headline: Galy brings lab-grown cocoa chocolate to US; bakers add fiber; FDA clears salt substitutes
summary: Galy will launch cell-cultured cocoa chocolate (WunderHaus) in the US in December: the first funded cocoa-alternative brand reaching this market, and both a partnership lead and a competitive signal for Belcolade.
Fibre is the bakery story of the day: Grupo Bimbo and Calise are adding fibre to everyday bread and rolls, a direct opening for Puratos fibre-enrichment solutions in North America.

Regulatory: FDA will allow salt substitutes in 139 standardized foods from December 14, 2026, giving bakery customers room to cut sodium, while HHS pressure on ultra-processed foods favours clean-label, fewer-additive formulations.
MOA Foodtech and Espiga I+D are partnering on egg replacement for bakery, a competitive signal for Patisserie's egg-replacer offer.
Science to watch: new sourdough starter consortia and an upcycled apple-pomace sourdough ingredient point to differentiated flavour and clean-label shelf life for Sapore.

items.title: Exclusive: Galy Expands Cell Culture Tech to Cocoa with US Launch of WunderHaus Chocolate Brand
items.summary: Boston biotech Galy (backed by Bill Gates and Sam Altman) is entering cell-cultured cocoa with the WunderHaus chocolate brand, launching in the US in December and the UAE in 2027.
items.why: A funded US cocoa-alternative player going to market now: a partnership or supply option for cocoa-free Belcolade lines, and a competitive signal.

items.title: MOA Foodtech and Espiga I+D partner on egg replacement for bakery
items.summary: Spanish start-up MOA Foodtech and Espiga I+D partner on egg replacement for bakery.
items.why: A start-up partnership targeting egg replacement in bakery and cakes: a direct competitive and partnership signal for Patisserie.

items.title: Grupo Bimbo focused on adding fiber to portfolio
items.summary: Grupo Bimbo is adding fibre across its portfolio, moving white bread toward 'fibre source' status.
items.why: The largest NA baker pushing fibre into white bread is a direct opportunity for fibre-enrichment solutions.

items.title: FDA Rule Will Allow Salt Substitutes in 139 Standardized Foods Starting December 14, 2026
items.summary: An FDA rule lets manufacturers use salt substitutes in 139 standardized foods from December 14, 2026.
items.why: Standardized breads and rolls are among the foods with salt in their standard, so bakery customers get a clear path to sodium reduction; a sell-in moment for salt-reduction solutions.

items.title: Upcycling apple pomace into a type III sourdough ingredient: effects on nutritional quality, antioxidant activity and bread shelf-life
items.summary: Brazilian researchers fermented apple pomace with L. plantarum into a type III sourdough ingredient; at 15-20% it raised fibre and antioxidants and extended mold-free shelf life of wheat bread.
items.why: An upcycled, clean-label sourdough ingredient that adds fibre and shelf life fits the Sapore/O-tentic range; worth tracking as a formulation idea.

items.title: Modulation of cocoa fermentation by co-inoculation of Pichia kluyveri CCMA0237 and Hanseniaspora uvarum CCMA0236: targeted chemical profiling and chocolate quality
items.summary: Co-inoculating Pichia kluyveri and Hanseniaspora uvarum starter yeasts steered cocoa fermentation chemistry and improved chocolate quality.
items.why: Starter cultures for cocoa fermentation are a lever for Belcolade flavour consistency and origin programmes.

items.title: Chocolate has a new problem. And it’s not cocoa prices
items.summary: Heatwaves are hitting cocoa supply and consumer demand; manufacturers are adapting formats and retail to protect sales.
items.why: Heat-resistant chocolate and format innovation is an opportunity for Belcolade customers.

items.title: Cross-feeding and stress response are the basis of increased fruitiness and leavening capacity of a new consortium of the sourdough microorganisms Companilactobacillus crustorum and Wickerhamomyces anomalus
items.summary: A new sourdough consortium (C. crustorum + W. anomalus) gives fruitier flavour and better leavening through cross-feeding and stress response.
items.why: A candidate starter culture for differentiated sourdough flavour; worth contacting the authors for Sapore.

items.title: From bean to bar 5.0: Artificial intelligence, sensing technologies and robotics across the cocoa–chocolate value chain
items.summary: Review of AI, sensing and robotics across the cocoa–chocolate value chain ('bean to bar 5.0').
items.why: A roadmap for digitalising Belcolade sourcing and processing.

items.title: Kemin guide offers roadmap to clean-label baking
items.summary: Kemin published a guide for clean-label bakery reformulation.
items.why: Competitor move in clean-label bakery; worth reviewing to benchmark Puratos's own clean-label messaging.

items.title: Calise Bakery introduces higher fiber rolls
items.summary: US bakery Calise launched higher-fibre rolls with lower net carbs, more protein and no artificial colours.
items.why: Shows NA demand for high-fibre, lower-carb rolls; a sell-in angle for fibre and protein bread solutions.

items.title: RFK Jr. Reportedly Pressing Agenda on Ultra-Processed Foods
items.summary: HHS Secretary RFK Jr. is reportedly pushing an agenda on ultra-processed foods.
items.why: A federal ultra-processed definition or labelling push would hit packaged bread, cakes and confectionery; clean-label, fewer-additive solutions gain value.

items.title: Louisville-developed sourdough appliance named one of Time's Best Inventions of 2026
items.summary: A Louisville-developed sourdough appliance was named one of Time's Best Inventions of 2026.
items.why: Consumer sourdough automation is gaining mainstream attention; a possible partner or channel for Sapore starters.

items.title: Antimicrobial mechanism of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LWQ17 against roping-forming Bacillus species and its application in preventing rope spoilage of Chinese steamed bread
items.summary: A L. plantarum strain inhibits rope-forming Bacillus and prevents rope spoilage in steamed bread.
items.why: Natural rope prevention is a clean-label alternative to propionate for Bakery shelf-life solutions.

items.title: Use of starch-modifying enzymes for enhanced bread quality and reduced in vitro starch hydrolysis
items.summary: Starch-modifying enzymes improved bread quality and lowered in-vitro starch digestibility.
items.why: Enzymes that both improve bread and lower glycemic response fit the S500 improver line.

items.title: Keeping surplus bread in the food system: Environmental and economic assessment of on-site upcycling in industrial bakeries
items.summary: Environmental and economic assessment of upcycling surplus bread on site at industrial bakeries.
items.why: Bread-waste upcycling is a service and ingredient opportunity for industrial bakery customers.

items.title: Preparation and application of soy protein isolate-filled sucrose composite particles in sugar-reduced chocolate via protein-mediated morphological modulation
items.summary: Soy-protein-filled sucrose composite particles cut sugar in chocolate while keeping sweetness.
items.why: A structured-sugar approach for sugar-reduced Belcolade lines; worth monitoring for licensing.

items.title: Unveiling the impact of mixed-strain solid-state fermentation on wheat bran dietary fiber: gluten protein structure evolution, dough rheological modulation and steamed bread quality enhancement
items.summary: Study of mixed-strain solid-state fermentation of wheat bran fibre and its effects on gluten structure, dough rheology and steamed bread quality.
items.why: Fermented bran is a route to high-fibre bread without the usual volume loss, relevant to Bakery fibre enrichment.

items.title: Effects of lactic acid bacteria and yeast co-fermentation in sourdough on the quality of whole-wheat bread
items.summary: Research on LAB and yeast co-fermentation in sourdough to improve whole-wheat bread quality.
items.why: Supports Bakery's sourdough and whole-grain portfolio with strain-pairing data.

items.title: Mixed-culture lactic acid fermentation attenuates bitterness and lowers the in vitro glycemic potential of Tartary buckwheat sourdough bread
items.summary: Mixed-culture lactic fermentation reduced bitterness and in-vitro glycemic potential of Tartary buckwheat sourdough bread.
items.why: Low-GI sourdough from alternative grains matches Bakery's health and sourdough priorities.

items.title: Cocoa and Chocolate Processing: Quality Changes, Monitoring Approaches, and Opportunities for Rapid and Non-Destructive Analysis Using Near Infrared Spectroscopy and Hyperspectral Imaging
items.summary: UNICAMP review of quality changes across cocoa/chocolate processing and NIR/hyperspectral imaging for rapid, non-destructive monitoring.
items.why: Inline NIR/HSI could tighten Belcolade process control; a good primer for plant digitalisation.

items.title: Development and evaluation of oat β-glucan enriched white wheat bread: physicochemical properties, sensory acceptance and effects on cardiometabolic risk markers in mildly hypercholesterolemic subjects with overweight/obesity.
items.summary: Greek clinical study: oat beta-glucan white bread (2.1 g/100 g) kept good sensory scores and improved lipid and inflammatory markers in overweight adults.
items.why: Clinical evidence for beta-glucan white bread supports health-claim-ready Bakery solutions; industry partner ELBISCO shows commercial interest.

items.title: Lactic acid bacterium F. sanfranciscensis impairs fitness of yeast M. humilis in a synthetic wheat sourdough medium
items.summary: INRAE/Melbourne study shows the sourdough bacterium F. sanfranciscensis reduces fitness of the yeast M. humilis, overturning the assumed cross-feeding relationship.
items.why: Fundamental insight for designing stable sourdough starter consortia (Sapore).

items.title: Foam-templated dual-network oleogels based on soybean protein isolate-κ-carrageenan and glycerol monostearate for partial cocoa butter replacement in a model chocolate
items.summary: Soy protein–carrageenan foam oleogels as partial cocoa butter replacement in model chocolate.
items.why: Cocoa butter replacers are strategic with cocoa prices high; early-stage but on-theme for Chocolate.

items.title: Beyond cocoa butter: How partial substitution with cocoa butter extenders reshapes temporal dominance of sensations and aroma release in chocolate
items.summary: Sensory study of how cocoa butter extenders change taste dominance and aroma release in chocolate.
items.why: Helps Chocolate gauge consumer-visible trade-offs of CBEs in cost-optimised recipes.

items.title: GLP-1 consumers still enjoying chocolate and candy
items.summary: NCA research finds GLP-1 users remain engaged with chocolate and candy.
items.why: GLP-1 consumers still buy chocolate; supports portion-controlled and better-for-you Belcolade formats.

items.title: Hershey, WCS launch $2.5m drive for deforestation-free Nigerian cocoa
items.summary: Hershey and WCS launched a $2.5m programme for deforestation-free Nigerian cocoa.
items.why: Competitor sustainability sourcing move; relevant benchmark for Cacao-Trace.

items.title: FDA Proposes Enforcement Discretion for Small Retailers and Restaurants Under the Food Traceability Rule
items.summary: FDA proposed enforcement discretion for small retailers and restaurants under the FSMA 204 food traceability rule.
items.why: Eases traceability work for some in-store bakery and foodservice customers, but larger customers will keep asking suppliers like Puratos for lot-level records.

items.title: What neuroscience reveals about functional bread
items.summary: How brain-activity measurement could help bakers understand reactions to functional bread texture, flavour and messaging.
items.why: Neuroscience-based sensory testing could strengthen Taste Tomorrow insights for functional bread.

items.title: APAC cocoa trends: ‘Worst is past’, but risks remain
items.summary: FoodNavigator: APAC cocoa market says the worst is past, but risks remain.
items.why: Cocoa price outlook affects Belcolade costing and customer demand for cocoa-saving recipes.

items.title: California Standardizes Food Date Labels: The First Statewide Mandate and What's Next
items.summary: California is the first state to mandate standardized food date labels.
items.why: Packaged bakery customers selling in California must switch to standard date wording, which ties into shelf-life claims and Puratos shelf-life solutions.

items.title: Same, same, but different: An updated overview of legal definitions of sourdough and sourdough breads in Europe
items.summary: Updated overview of legal definitions of sourdough and sourdough bread across Europe.
items.why: Labelling rules directly affect how Sapore-based breads can be marketed; useful for regulatory teams.

items.title: Type 3 sourdough productions with Lactobacillus amylovorus DCE 471 and Companilactobacillus paralimentarius IMDO 1Mg105
items.summary: Type 3 sourdough production with L. amylovorus and C. paralimentarius strains (IMDO, Brussels).
items.why: Industrial type 3 sourdough research from a Belgian lab: a natural collaboration partner for Sapore.

items.title: Linking fat structure and rheology to laminated pastry performance
items.summary: Study links fat structure and rheology to laminated pastry performance.
items.why: Useful science for laminating fats and croissant performance.

items.title: Solid fat content–dependent regulation of protein–starch conformations and water–lipid migration in laminated pastry during thermal processing
items.summary: Solid fat content changes protein-starch structure and water-lipid migration in laminated pastry during baking.

items.title: Trehalose mitigates freeze–thaw-induced gluten network deterioration by modulating aggregation behavior and molecular conformation
items.summary: Trehalose limits freeze-thaw damage to the gluten network.
items.why: A possible route to more robust frozen dough.

items.title: Defending Label Claims Built on FDA Enforcement Discretion: Allulose After Franco v. Chobani
items.summary: A law-firm analysis of label claims that rely on FDA enforcement discretion for allulose, after Franco v. Chobani.
items.why: Sugar-reduced fillings and chocolate using allulose face litigation risk on 'sugar' labelling; worth a check with regulatory before claims are made.

items.title: Better Dairy eyeing US market with GRAS notice
items.summary: Better Dairy filed a GRAS notice to bring precision-fermented, animal-free dairy ingredients to the US.
items.why: A GRAS step toward animal-free dairy for creams and fillings; a supplier to watch for dairy-free Patisserie.

items.title: Fiber adds nutritional value, permission for indulgence
items.summary: Adding fibre to sweet treats helps consumers close a nutrition gap.
items.why: Supports fibre-enriched cake and sweet-goods positioning for Patisserie.

items.title: The Gluten-Free Landscape: Consumer Demand Meets Regulatory Change
items.summary: Gluten-free demand and changing gluten-free labelling rules.
items.why: Relevant to gluten-free bread mixes and claims for Bakery customers.

items.title: NAMA president sees opportunities amid milling industry headwinds
items.summary: The North American Millers' Association president on milling industry headwinds and opportunities.
items.why: Flour supply and policy context for Bakery customers.
